body:
ONE QUESTION, ANSWERABLE ON PAPER, THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE FILM PATH IS A SIX-WEEK ARCHITECTURE
PROJECT OR A MUCH SHORTER ONE.

CAN SHERLOCK'S EXISTING VIDEO ANNOTATIONS SERVE AS THE SOURCE REPRESENTATION?

THE OWNER'S OBSERVATION THAT PROMPTED THIS: film recall data is open and abundant while our
best-matched text corpus is blocked on a credential. That is a real asymmetry and it inverts the
priority I set this afternoon.

THE IDEA THE OWNER'S FRAMING SURFACED, which I had not had: FOR FILM WE DO NOT NEED THE VIDEO, WE
NEED A SOURCE REPRESENTATION. ContextLab's sherlock-topic-model-paper ships 17 raw participant
recalls together with VIDEO ANNOTATIONS AND DERIVED EVENT DATA. Somebody has already segmented
that film into events. If that annotation can stand as the source side, the entire
film-licensing problem root's ADR was wrestling with -- copyright-controlled stimulus, no
redistributable source -- is sidestepped, because we never touch the video.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH, docs only, no fetch of participant text into the repository:

  1. WHAT THE ANNOTATIONS ACTUALLY ARE. Event boundaries? Scene labels? Per-event descriptions?
     Timestamps only, or content? An event LIST is not a NarrativeGraph, and the gap between them
     is the whole cost estimate.
  2. CAN THEY CARRY WHAT OUR SOURCE SIDE NEEDS -- situations, participants, relations, hierarchy
     -- or only ordering? If only ordering, say so; a source that supports temporal alignment and
     nothing else is still useful and is a much smaller claim.
  3. THE METHODOLOGICAL COST, and it must be stated in the artifact rather than discovered later:
     ALIGNING TO SOMEONE ELSE'S EVENT ANNOTATION MEANS MEASURING RECALL AGAINST THEIR EVENT MODEL,
     NOT OURS. Much of this literature does exactly that. It is defensible and it is a DERIVATION,
     not an observed source, and every number computed against it inherits their segmentation
     decisions.
  4. LICENCE on the annotations specifically. The repository is public; the episode is not. Those
     are different objects with possibly different terms.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT: the film ADR. Root has stage A on the film-source-representation topic --
locator versus denominator versus absence-erasing derivation, the presentation-axis design, the
typed denominator carrying its source kind. That work stands and this does not replace it. This
answers a narrower and more urgent question: IS THERE A USABLE SOURCE SIDE AT ALL, without which
the architecture has nothing to represent.

AND IT DOES NOT AVOID STAGE 1b. RecallSegmenter.segment(transcript: StorySource) -- recalls are
TEXT whatever the source medium is. Film changes what the SOURCE is, not what the RECALL is, so
the proposition provider at 4 of 50 is needed either way. Anyone arguing film as a way around the
provider problem has the dependency backwards.

FilmFestival (OpenNeuro ds004042) is NOT the candidate here: it has recall onset, duration and
transcript, but no source-side annotation. Sherlock specifically.

Unassigned. Docs only. Volunteer on coordination.
